mission:
Build a small work-log reporting library in plain ESM JavaScript with node:test tests and no dependencies.
1. src/duration.js: `parseDuration(text)` returns seconds. Accept "90s", "15m", "2h", combined forms like "1h30m" and "1h 30m 15s", and decimals like "1.5h". Reject empty strings, unknown units, negative values, repeated units ("1h2h") and out-of-order units ("30m1h") with a TypeError. Also `formatDuration(seconds)` producing the shortest canonical form ("1h30m", "45s", "0s").
2. src/csv.js: `parseCsvLine(line)` returns an array of fields following RFC 4180 for a single line: quoted fields, commas inside quotes, doubled quotes as an escaped quote, empty fields, and surrounding whitespace preserved inside quotes but trimmed outside. Throw a SyntaxError on an unterminated quote or on text after a closing quote.
3. src/table.js: `formatTable(rows)` renders an array of string arrays as an aligned plain-text table with a header separator; columns are padded to the widest cell; numbers-only columns are right-aligned.
4. src/report.js: `buildReport(csvText)` takes CSV text with a header "person,task,duration", uses parseCsvLine and parseDuration to total the time per person, and returns the text produced by formatTable with columns person, tasks, total (formatted with formatDuration), sorted by total descending then person. Lines that fail to parse are collected and listed after the table as "skipped line N: reason". This task depends on the duration, csv and table modules.
The repository has docs/CONVENTIONS.md; follow it. If a task turns out to need something that no planned task provides, propose the missing task through the graph-change tool instead of doing unplanned work in your own task.
Each module is a separate task with its own test file under test/. The report task must start only after the modules it uses are finished. Authors of duration, csv and table must tell the report task the exact exported signatures and error behaviour through a message. `npm test` must pass.

plan.summary: Build worklog-kit's reporting library as four plain-ESM modules (src/duration.js, src/csv.js, src/table.js, src/report.js) plus src/config.js, which docs/CONVENTIONS.md line 3 requires for any module that formats output for people and says must be its own small task with a test. The repository today holds only package.json ("type": "module", test script `node --test`, no dependencies), src/index.js (VERSION export), test/index.test.js, README.md and docs/CONVENTIONS.md; none of those are modified. The plan starts from Planner A and has five tasks: config, duration and csv run in parallel on disjoint files; table follows config; report starts only after duration, csv and table are finished and have each messaged it their exact signatures and error behaviour. Critique fixes applied: parseDuration rounds to whole seconds so formatDuration never receives a fraction; the CSV quote-in-unquoted-field case is decided up front (literal character); a malformed header is a SyntaxError; the layout between table and skipped lines is fixed; module tasks verify with their own test file rather than the whole suite, and the full `npm test` run is the report task's closing step.
assumptions: SEPARATOR is ' | ' (space, pipe, space). docs/CONVENTIONS.md fixes the name and location (`src/config.js`, `export const SEPARATOR`) but not the value.
Only src/table.js needs SEPARATOR directly; src/report.js gets its columns through formatTable and its 'skipped line N: reason' lines have no columns.
Code style follows src/index.js and test/index.test.js: single quotes, no semicolons, `import test from 'node:test'`, `import assert from 'node:assert/strict'`.
src/index.js is not changed; no re-exports were requested.

parseDuration: lowercase units h, m, s only, in that order, each at most once; whitespace allowed between components and at the ends but not between a number and its unit; the total is rounded with Math.round to whole seconds (so '1.5s' is 2 and '0.4s' is 0). The rounding is not in the request; it is added so per-person totals are always integers that formatDuration accepts.
formatDuration accepts only non-negative integers (TypeError otherwise) and emits non-zero components in h, m, s order without spaces; 0 gives '0s'; hours are not capped.

parseCsvLine keeps a double quote that appears after other non-whitespace text in an unquoted field as a literal character, because the request names only two SyntaxError cases. Whitespace around a quoted field is discarded.

formatTable treats rows[0] as the header; a column is numbers-only when there is at least one body row and every body cell matches /^-?\d+(\.\d+)?$/; the header cell follows the column's alignment; every cell is fully padded (no trailing-whitespace trimming); the header rule is dashes per column width joined with SEPARATOR; no trailing newline.

In buildReport, 'tasks' is the number of successfully parsed lines for that person; N in 'skipped line N' is the 1-based line number in the input with the header as line 1; blank lines are ignored but still counted; a missing or wrong header throws SyntaxError; skipped lines follow the table after one blank line.
Whether parallel tasks share one working tree is unknown, so module tasks verify with their own test file instead of the whole suite.
The baseline `npm test` was not run during synthesis (the planner hook allows only read-only inspection); the critique reports it passes with 1 test.
acceptanceCriteria: `npm test` exits 0 with zero failing tests and runs test/index.test.js, test/config.test.js, test/duration.test.js, test/csv.test.js, test/table.test.js and test/report.test.js.

src/duration.js exports parseDuration and formatDuration; src/csv.js exports parseCsvLine; src/table.js exports formatTable; src/report.js exports buildReport; src/config.js exports SEPARATOR; each behaves as the request specifies.
src/table.js imports SEPARATOR from src/config.js and contains no hard-coded column separator (docs/CONVENTIONS.md line 3).
No module throws a plain Error for bad input; only TypeError or SyntaxError (docs/CONVENTIONS.md line 4).
package.json is unchanged (no dependencies or devDependencies, test script `node --test`); src/index.js and test/index.test.js are unchanged; no test is deleted, skipped or weakened.
src/report.js imports and uses parseCsvLine, parseDuration, formatDuration and formatTable rather than re-implementing them.

buildReport on a sample CSV returns the formatTable output with columns person, tasks, total sorted by total descending then person, followed by 'skipped line N: reason' lines for lines that fail to parse.
The duration, csv and table tasks each sent a message to the report task stating exact exported signatures and error behaviour.

tasks.title: Implement src/duration.js (parseDuration, formatDuration) with tests
tasks.description:
Repository: worklog-kit, plain ESM JavaScript (package.json "type": "module", test script `node --test`, no dependencies allowed). Follow docs/CONVENTIONS.md: errors for bad input are TypeError or SyntaxError, never plain Error. Match the style of src/index.js and test/index.test.js: single quotes, no semicolons, `import test from 'node:test'`, `import assert from 'node:assert/strict'`.

Create src/duration.js exporting two named functions.

`parseDuration(text)` returns a whole number of seconds.
- Components are `<number><unit>` with unit h, m or s (lowercase only). The number is a non-negative decimal such as `2`, `1.5`, `0.25` (digits, optionally a dot and more digits; no sign, no exponent, no leading dot).
- Each unit appears at most once, in the order h, m, s. Whitespace is allowed between components and at the start and end, but not between a number and its unit.
- Examples: '90s' -> 90, '15m' -> 900, '2h' -> 7200, '1h30m' -> 5400, '1h 30m 15s' -> 5415, '1.5h' -> 5400, '0s' -> 0.
- The total is rounded to the nearest whole second with Math.round: '1.5s' -> 2, '0.4s' -> 0. This is deliberate, so that sums of parsed durations are always integers that formatDuration accepts.
- Throw TypeError for: non-string input, empty or whitespace-only string, unknown units ('5d', '10x'), a number with no unit ('10'), negative values ('-5m'), repeated units ('1h2h'), out-of-order units ('30m1h'), uppercase units ('1H'), and any other malformed text ('h', '1hh', '1h foo'). Messages must be short, descriptive and include the offending input (for example `invalid duration: "30m1h"`), because src/report.js prints error.message as the reason for a skipped line.

`formatDuration(seconds)` returns the shortest canonical form.
- The argument must be a non-negative integer number; otherwise throw TypeError (negative, fractional, NaN, Infinity, non-number).
- Concatenate the non-zero components in h, m, s order with no spaces: 5400 -> '1h30m', 45 -> '45s', 0 -> '0s', 90 -> '1m30s', 3600 -> '1h', 3661 -> '1h1m1s', 7205 -> '2h5s'. Hours are not capped (90000 -> '25h').

Create test/duration.test.js covering every example and every rejection case above (assert.throws with TypeError), plus a round trip parseDuration(formatDuration(n)) === n for several integers.

Touch only src/duration.js and test/duration.test.js. Verify with `node --test test/duration.test.js test/index.test.js`. Do not use the whole suite as your pass/fail check: other tasks are writing other files at the same time. If a file owned by another task is broken, report it by message; do not fix it. If you find you need something no planned task provides, propose the missing task through the graph-change tool (mcp__nexus__propose_graph_change) instead of doing unplanned work.

When done, you must send a message with mcp__nexus__send_message (type 'handoff', toTask 'report') stating: the import path, the exact exported signatures and return types, the Math.round rule, that formatDuration requires a non-negative integer, which inputs throw, that the error type is TypeError, and what error.message looks like.
acceptanceCriteria: src/duration.js exports `parseDuration` and `formatDuration` as named exports and imports nothing from outside the repository.
parseDuration returns 90, 900, 7200, 5400, 5415, 5400 for '90s', '15m', '2h', '1h30m', '1h 30m 15s', '1.5h', and returns 2 for '1.5s' and 0 for '0.4s'.
parseDuration throws TypeError (not plain Error) for '', '   ', '5d', '10', '-5m', '1h2h', '30m1h', '1H' and non-string input, and the message includes the offending input.
formatDuration returns '1h30m', '45s', '0s', '1m30s', '1h' for 5400, 45, 0, 90, 3600 and throws TypeError for -1, 1.5, NaN and '10'.
test/duration.test.js covers the cases above and `node --test test/duration.test.js` passes.
Only src/duration.js and test/duration.test.js are changed.
A handoff message with exact signatures, the rounding rule and error behaviour was sent to task 'report'.

tasks.title: Implement src/csv.js (parseCsvLine) with tests
tasks.description:
Repository: worklog-kit, plain ESM JavaScript (package.json "type": "module", test script `node --test`, no dependencies allowed). Follow docs/CONVENTIONS.md: errors for bad input are TypeError or SyntaxError, never plain Error. Match the style of src/index.js and test/index.test.js: single quotes, no semicolons, `import test from 'node:test'`, `import assert from 'node:assert/strict'`.

Create src/csv.js exporting the named function `parseCsvLine(line)`, which returns an array of string fields for a single CSV line following RFC 4180. Write it as a small character-by-character state machine, not a split on commas. The input is one line; do not handle multi-line records.

Rules:
- Fields are separated by commas: 'a,b,c' -> ['a','b','c'].
- Empty fields are kept: 'a,,c' -> ['a','','c']; ',' -> ['','']; 'a,' -> ['a','']; '' -> [''].
- A field whose first non-whitespace character is a double quote is a quoted field. Inside it commas are literal ('"a,b",c' -> ['a,b','c']) and a doubled quote is one literal quote ('"say ""hi"""' -> ['say "hi"']). '""' -> [''].
- Whitespace inside quotes is preserved; whitespace outside quotes is trimmed: '  a  , b ' -> ['a','b']; ' " a " ,b' -> [' a ','b']. Whitespace between a comma and an opening quote, or between a closing quote and the next comma or end of line, is discarded (this also covers a trailing '\r').
- Throw SyntaxError on an unterminated quote ('"abc', 'a,"b').
- Throw SyntaxError when non-whitespace text follows a closing quote before the next comma ('"a"b', '"a" b,c').
- A double quote that appears after other non-whitespace text in an unquoted field is kept as a literal character ('ab"c' -> ['ab"c']). This is deliberate: the request names only the two error cases above.
- Throw TypeError if `line` is not a string.
- Messages must be short and descriptive (for example 'unterminated quote', 'unexpected text after closing quote'), because src/report.js prints error.message as the reason for a skipped line.

Create test/csv.test.js covering every example above with assert.deepEqual, both SyntaxError cases with assert.throws(..., SyntaxError), and the TypeError case.

Touch only src/csv.js and test/csv.test.js. Verify with `node --test test/csv.test.js test/index.test.js`. Do not use the whole suite as your pass/fail check: other tasks are writing other files at the same time. If a file owned by another task is broken, report it by message; do not fix it. If you find you need something no planned task provides, propose the missing task through the graph-change tool (mcp__nexus__propose_graph_change) instead of doing unplanned work.

When done, you must send a message with mcp__nexus__send_message (type 'handoff', toTask 'report') stating: the import path, the exact exported signature and return shape, the trimming rules, what '' returns, the literal-quote rule, and exactly which inputs throw which error type with which message.
acceptanceCriteria: src/csv.js exports `parseCsvLine` as a named export and imports nothing from outside the repository.
parseCsvLine returns ['a','b','c'], ['a','','c'], ['a,b','c'], ['say "hi"'], [''] for 'a,b,c', 'a,,c', '"a,b",c', '"say ""hi"""', ''.
Whitespace outside quotes is trimmed and whitespace inside quotes is preserved: ' " a " ,b' -> [' a ','b'] and '  a  , b ' -> ['a','b'].
'"abc' and '"a"b' each throw SyntaxError; non-string input throws TypeError; no plain Error is thrown.
'ab"c' returns ['ab"c'].
test/csv.test.js covers the cases above and `node --test test/csv.test.js` passes.
Only src/csv.js and test/csv.test.js are changed.
A handoff message with the exact signature and error behaviour was sent to task 'report'.

tasks.title: Implement src/table.js (formatTable) with tests
tasks.description:
Repository: worklog-kit, plain ESM JavaScript (package.json "type": "module", test script `node --test`, no dependencies allowed). Match the style of src/index.js and test/index.test.js: single quotes, no semicolons, `import test from 'node:test'`, `import assert from 'node:assert/strict'`.

Follow docs/CONVENTIONS.md: (1) every module that formats output for people takes its column separator from src/config.js, which the dependency task 'config' has created as `export const SEPARATOR = ' | '`. Use `import { SEPARATOR } from './config.js'` and do not hard-code a separator. Do not modify src/config.js. (2) Errors for bad input are TypeError or SyntaxError, never plain Error.

Create src/table.js exporting the named function `formatTable(rows)`. `rows` is an array of string arrays; rows[0] is the header.
- Each column is padded to the width of its widest cell, header included.
- Cells in a line are joined with SEPARATOR.
- After the header line comes one separator line: '-' repeated to each column's width, joined with SEPARATOR.
- A column is numbers-only when there is at least one body row and every body cell in it (header excluded) matches /^-?\d+(\.\d+)?$/. Such a column is right-aligned (padStart), header cell included. Every other column is left-aligned (padEnd). An empty cell is not a number.
- Every cell is fully padded; do not trim trailing whitespace. Lines are joined with '\n' and there is no trailing newline.
- Rows shorter than the widest row are treated as having empty strings for the missing cells.
- A header-only table returns the header line and the separator line.
- Throw TypeError if rows is not a non-empty array of arrays of strings.

Example with SEPARATOR ' | ': formatTable([['person','tasks','total'],['alice','2','1h30m'],['bob','10','45s']]) returns the four lines
`person | tasks | total`
`------ | ----- | -----`
`alice  |     2 | 1h30m`
`bob    |    10 | 45s  `

Create test/table.test.js. Build expected strings from the imported SEPARATOR rather than a literal ' | '. Cover: padding to the widest cell, the header separator line, right alignment of a numbers-only column including its header, left alignment of a mixed column, a short row, a header-only table, no trailing newline, and the TypeError cases.

Touch only src/table.js and test/table.test.js. Verify with `node --test test/table.test.js test/config.test.js test/index.test.js`. Do not use the whole suite as your pass/fail check: other tasks may still be writing other files. If a file owned by another task is broken, report it by message; do not fix it. If you find you need something no planned task provides, propose the missing task through the graph-change tool (mcp__nexus__propose_graph_change) instead of doing unplanned work.

When done, you must send a message with mcp__nexus__send_message (type 'handoff', toTask 'report') stating: the import path, the exact exported signature, the expected input shape, the exact output layout (separator, header rule, alignment rule, full padding, no trailing newline, header-only output), and exactly which inputs throw TypeError.
acceptanceCriteria: src/table.js exports `formatTable` as a named export, imports SEPARATOR from './config.js', and contains no hard-coded column separator literal.
For the example in the description, formatTable returns exactly the four lines shown, joined with '\n' and without a trailing newline.
A numbers-only column is right-aligned including its header; a column with any non-numeric body cell is left-aligned.
A header-only input returns exactly two lines: the header and the dash separator.
formatTable throws TypeError (not plain Error) for a non-array, an empty array, and a row containing a non-string cell.
test/table.test.js builds its expectations from the imported SEPARATOR and `node --test test/table.test.js` passes.
Only src/table.js and test/table.test.js are changed.
A handoff message with the exact signature, output layout and error behaviour was sent to task 'report'.

tasks.title: Implement src/report.js (buildReport) with tests and run the full suite
tasks.description:
Repository: worklog-kit, plain ESM JavaScript (package.json "type": "module", test script `node --test`, no dependencies allowed). Follow docs/CONVENTIONS.md: errors for bad input are TypeError or SyntaxError, never plain Error. Match the style of src/index.js and test/index.test.js: single quotes, no semicolons, `import test from 'node:test'`, `import assert from 'node:assert/strict'`.

The dependency tasks have created src/duration.js (`parseDuration(text)` -> whole seconds, TypeError on bad input; `formatDuration(seconds)` -> string, requires a non-negative integer), src/csv.js (`parseCsvLine(line)` -> string[], SyntaxError on an unterminated quote or text after a closing quote) and src/table.js (`formatTable(rows)` -> string, rows[0] is the header, no trailing newline). Before writing code, read the handoff messages from tasks 'duration', 'csv' and 'table' and the three source files, and use the real signatures and error behaviour. If they differ from this description in a way that blocks you, send a message to the owning task or propose a graph change through mcp__nexus__propose_graph_change; do not edit those modules yourself.

Create src/report.js exporting the named function `buildReport(csvText)`. It must import and use parseCsvLine, parseDuration, formatDuration and formatTable; do not re-implement them.
- Throw TypeError if csvText is not a string.
- Split the text into lines on /\r?\n/. Line numbers are 1-based positions in the input.
- Line 1 is the header. Parse it with parseCsvLine; the fields must be exactly ['person','task','duration']. Otherwise throw SyntaxError (this includes empty input).
- For each later line: a blank or whitespace-only line is ignored but still counts in the numbering. Otherwise parse it with parseCsvLine, require exactly 3 fields, require a non-empty person, and parse the third field with parseDuration. A line that fails any of these is not thrown; it is recorded as `skipped line N: reason`. When parseCsvLine or parseDuration threw, reason is that error's message. For a wrong field count the reason is `expected 3 fields, got K`. For an empty person the reason is `missing person`.
- For each person, add up the seconds and count the valid lines (the 'tasks' column, as a decimal string).
- Rows are sorted by total seconds descending, then by person ascending using plain string comparison (<).
- The table is formatTable([['person','tasks','total'], ...rows]) with total rendered by formatDuration.
- Return value: with no skipped lines, exactly the formatTable output. With skipped lines, the formatTable output, then one empty line, then the skipped lines in input order, one per line; that is `table + '\n\n' + skipped.join('\n')`. No trailing newline in either case.
- With a header and no valid data lines the table is the header-only table.

Create test/report.test.js. Build expected tables by calling formatTable on the expected rows, rather than hard-coding the separator. Cover: totals and task counts over several lines per person; sort by total descending; a tie on total broken by person; a decimal duration such as '1.5h' and a sub-second one such as '1.5s' contributing to a total without throwing; a quoted task containing a comma; CRLF input giving the same result as LF input; a blank line ignored but counted in numbering; skipped lines for an unterminated quote, a bad duration, a wrong field count and an empty person, each with the right N and listed in input order after one empty line; exact reason text for the two reasons this module owns, and a non-empty reason for the ones coming from the other modules; output with no skipped lines equal to the table alone; header-only input; SyntaxError for a wrong or missing header; TypeError for non-string input.

Touch only src/report.js and test/report.test.js. Finish by running `npm test` from the repository root: all six test files (index, config, duration, csv, table, report) must run and pass. If a failure is in a file owned by another task, report it by message with the failing output instead of fixing it.
acceptanceCriteria: src/report.js exports `buildReport` as a named export and imports parseCsvLine from './csv.js', parseDuration and formatDuration from './duration.js', and formatTable from './table.js'.

For input 'person,task,duration
bob,a,30m
alice,b,1h
alice,c,30m' buildReport returns formatTable([['person','tasks','total'],['alice','2','1h30m'],['bob','1','30m']]).
Two people with equal totals appear in ascending person order; otherwise rows are in descending total order.

A line with an unterminated quote, a bad duration, a wrong field count or an empty person is not thrown; it appears after the table and one empty line as `skipped line N: reason`, with N the 1-based input line number (header is line 1), in input order.
With no skipped lines the result equals the table alone; the result never ends with a newline.
CRLF input produces the same result as the same text with LF; blank lines are ignored but counted in line numbering.
A decimal duration such as '1.5s' in a valid line does not make buildReport throw.
A wrong or missing header throws SyntaxError; non-string input throws TypeError; no plain Error is thrown.

test/report.test.js covers the cases above, and `npm test` exits 0 with test/index.test.js, test/config.test.js, test/duration.test.js, test/csv.test.js, test/table.test.js and test/report.test.js all passing.
Only src/report.js and test/report.test.js are changed by this task; package.json, src/index.js and test/index.test.js are unchanged in the repository.

risks.description: parseDuration accepts decimals while formatDuration rejects non-integers, so a fractional per-person total would make buildReport throw on a line that parsed successfully.
risks.mitigation: parseDuration rounds its total with Math.round (tested with '1.5s' -> 2 and '0.4s' -> 0), and the report task has a test with a sub-second decimal duration. The rounding rule is stated in the duration handoff message and in the assumptions so the user can object.

risks.description: `npm test` is `node --test`, which discovers every test file. If parallel tasks share one working tree, a module task could fail on a sibling's half-written file that it is not allowed to touch.
risks.mitigation: config, duration, csv and table verify with their own test file plus test/index.test.js. The full `npm test` run belongs to the report task, which starts after all the others. Workers are told to report failures in other tasks' files by message rather than fix them.

risks.description: The report task could be written against a contract that differs from what the module authors actually built, for example different error messages or table layout.
risks.mitigation: The grammar and layout decisions are fixed in the task descriptions; each module task must send a handoff message to 'report'; the report task reads both the messages and the source files first, builds expected tables through formatTable, and asserts exact reason text only for the reasons it owns.

risks.description: Several behaviours are planner decisions the request does not settle: SEPARATOR value ' | ', a literal quote inside an unquoted CSV field, full padding of the last column, 'tasks' as a count of valid lines, the blank line before skipped lines, and SyntaxError for a bad header.
risks.mitigation: Each is listed in the assumptions, written into one task only, and covered by a test, so changing any of them is a local edit to one module and its test.

risks.description: src/config.js is needed by table but not asked for in the request, so a worker could create it ad hoc inside the table task, against docs/CONVENTIONS.md line 3.
risks.mitigation: It is planned up front as the 'config' task with its own test, table depends on it, and table is told not to modify src/config.js. Every task is told to propose a graph change if it needs something no planned task provides.

error.why: The only failed criterion (duration, csv and table each sent a handoff message to report) cannot be repaired from the report task: it requires those three tasks to send their own messages. No code change in src/report.js or test/report.test.js is warranted.
